description: We are Pioneer Matrix from Ahmedabad, competing in the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Our vision is to democratize deep-space discovery with SphereX, an open-source, browser-based platform that makes NASA’s 102-band infrared sky surveys accessible to everyone. By empowering citizen scientists to visually explore multi-epoch cosmic shifts, we aim to turn everyday curiosity into active participation in uncovering the universe's hidden wonders.
summary:
Mission Visualizer is an open-source, browser-based astronomical exploration platform designed for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Analyzing multi-epoch near-infrared survey data from NASA’s SPSPHEREx HEREx space telescope (102 spectral bands from 0.75–5.0 µm on a 6-month cadence) typically requires downloading and processing massive raw FITS files. Our platform removes that barrier for both citizen scientists and researchers.

Users can query any sky coordinate, astronomical name, or Earth location to fetch and clean Caltech IRSA FITS data on demand. Through three interactive visual modes—Single Epoch, a Clyde Tombaugh Blink Comparator, and Difference Imaging—alongside Gaia DR3/CatWISE cross-matching, users can immediately isolate high-proper-motion targets like brown dwarfs, asteroids, and potential Planet X candidates, as well as variable stars. Paired with a unified 102-band molecular spectral graph and an adaptive AI assistant, our tool democratizes infrared sky discovery directly in the browser.
details:
SPHEREx Mission Visualizer is an interactive, browser-based astronomical discovery engine built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Planet X & SPHEREx track) by Team Pioneer Matrix. Every six months, NASA’s SPHEREx space telescope maps over 1 billion objects across 102 near-infrared spectral bands, yet raw multi-extension FITS files are bloated with zodiacal light interference, take 1–3 minutes to download and parse, and cannot render natively in standard web browsers. Our platform bridges professional astrophysical archives and citizen science—turning live Caltech IRSA telemetry into sub-millisecond visual and spectroscopic discovery with zero coding or desktop software required.

How It Works

  • Live FITS-to-JSON Pipeline: Using a Python FastAPI backend with astroquery, the platform queries the NASA/IPAC Caltech IRSA TAP archive on demand without requiring API keys. It automatically subtracts zodiacal background light, strips sky noise using a 3-sigma floor, applies a log1p stretch, and caches 128×128 grids into lightweight JSON.
    1. Single Epoch: False-color near-infrared rendering via ImageData.
    2. Blink Comparator: Cycles 6-month survey epochs at 1–8 fps to expose proper motion visually.
    3. Difference Imaging: Subtracts Epoch 1 from Epoch 2 to isolate moving objects as cyan (old position) and amber (new position) dipoles.
  • Astrometric HUD & 102-Band Spectroscopy: Clicking any source locks a corner-bracket targeting reticle, draws its proper motion vector, cross-references Gaia DR3 and CatWISE2020 in real time to flag uncataloged infrared candidates, and plots its full 102-band spectral energy distribution with automated absorption dip markers for
  • SPHEREx AI Analyzer: An integrated Gemini 2.5 Flash assistant that reads live target telemetry and astrometric metadata, offering a plain-English Casual Mode for students and explorers alongside a technical Deep Mode for researchers.

Creativity & Design Considerations Rather than building another static data table or complex scientific interface, we designed a minimalist, zero-clutter Swiss-editorial dark UI optimized for visual pattern recognition. To make high-dimensional infrared astronomy intuitive, we combined time-domain blink/dipole motion detection with live chemical fingerprinting and a token-efficient, context-aware AI guide—allowing anyone to separate known background stars from uncataloged brown dwarfs or outer solar system Planet X candidates in seconds.

Tools, Languages & Hardware Used

  • Frontend: HTML5 Canvas (ImageData rendering), Vanilla JavaScript, CSS3 (minimalist dark UI).
  • Backend & Astrophysics Stack: Python, FastAPI, astroquery, NumPy, Astropy (FITS parsing, 3-sigma noise filtering, log1p stretching).
  • Data Archives & APIs: NASA/IPAC Caltech IRSA TAP Archive, ESA Gaia DR3, NASA/IPAC CatWISE2020, CDS Sesame Name Resolver, OpenStreetMap Nominatim, and Google Gemini 2.5 Flash API.
  • Validation & Testing: Stress-tested against five verified astrophysical benchmarks—Barnard's Star Epsilon Indi , RW Aurigae, and R Draconis (245-day Mira variable)—supported by an automated Python unit test suite.

Benefits & Intended Impact By eliminating the 1–3 minute data-wrangling barrier and translating raw 102-band infrared arrays into instant visual dipoles and molecular profiles, SPHEREx Mission Visualizer democratizes access to NASA’s all-sky survey. It empowers students, educators, and citizen scientists worldwide to actively hunt for high-proper-motion substellar objects and outer solar system bodies directly from a web browser.
